summary: France is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the 63 countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (as of 30 December 2025) can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90, applied for via the official France-Visas portal.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for France?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit France and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a France Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11, applied for via the official France-Visas portal. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter France?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once ETIAS starts, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: How do I stay in France longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: You need a national long-stay visa (Type D), applied for via France-Visas before travel: €99, or €50 for students whose application went through a Centre pour les études en France. Many long-stay visas (VLS-TS) double as residence permits and must be validated online within 3 months of arrival.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for France?
faq.answer: Yes. France lists insurance covering medical and hospital costs in France, with minimum cover of €30,000, among the conditions every non-EU visitor must meet at the border, visa-free or not. Schengen visa applicants must also show travel medical insurance of at least €30,000 valid throughout the Schengen Area for the whole stay.
